title: A partial Fourier bound for the rank of tripartitioning tensors
statement: For integers a, b, c ≥ 0 with n = a+b+c ≥ 1 let T_{a,b,c} = Σ x_A y_B z_C over all ordered partitions (A, B, C) of [n] with |A| = a, |B| = b, |C| = c (P_d = T_{d,d,d} is Pratt's T_d and the P_d of Björklund–Kaski–Koana–Nederlof), and D_{a,b} = {S ⊕ T : |S| = a, |T| = b}, of size Σ_{j=0}^{min(a,b)} C(n, a+b−2j). (1) Over every field of characteristic ≠ 2, T_{a,b,c} = Σ_{l=1}^{|D_{a,b}|} u_{t_l} ⊗ u_{t_l} ⊗ W_l for suitable sign vectors t_l ∈ {±1}^n and vectors W_l, where u_t(S) = Π_{i∈S} t_i; hence R(T_{a,b,c}) ≤ |D_{a,b}|. For |a−b| ≤ 1 an explicit choice (t_n = +1 and at most min(a+b, n−1) entries −1) gives an integer identity 2^r T_{a,b,c} = Σ u_t ⊗ u_t ⊗ W̃_t, valid over every ring with 2 invertible. In particular R(P_d) ≤ Σ_{k=0}^{d} C(3d,2k) (4, 31, 247, 1981, ...), the bound of Flavi–Jelisiejew–Michałek (Proposition 6.18, there over algebraically closed fields of characteristic 0), and R(T_{1,1,c}) ≤ C(c+2,2)+1. (2) If |a−b| ≤ 1, every decomposition of this form (the same sign vector t in two factors, arbitrary third factor; over any field) has at least |D_{a,b}| terms; the same holds for any two factors whose sizes differ by at most 1. (3) D_d = |D_{d,d}| satisfies 8^d/2 − (27/4)^d ≤ D_d ≤ 8^d/2, so D_d/(8^d/2) → 1, D_d^{1/d} → 8 and log D_d / log C(3d,d) → 1/H(1/3).

bases: Flavi–Jelisiejew–Michałek 2025, arXiv:2408.02754v2, Proposition 6.18 (6.17 in v1), IMRN rnaf277: R(P_k) ≤ Σ_{j=0}^{k} C(3k,2j) over algebraically closed fields of characteristic 0

sources.authors: Flavi, C.; Jelisiejew, J.; Michałek, M.
sources.title: Symmetric powers: structure, smoothability, and applications
sources.note: Base of the note. arXiv v2 (29 August 2025) §6 read; the IMRN text was not read. Proposition 6.18 (v2, p. 31; Proposition 6.17 in v1): the rank of Pratt's tensor T_N, N = 3k, is at most ½ 8^k − Σ_{i=k+1}^{⌊N/2⌋} C(N, 2i) = Σ_{j=0}^{k} C(3k,2j), proved (p. 32) by bounding the rank by the number of symmetric differences of two k-subsets (group tensor of Z_2 and the substitution method); standing assumption (§2, p. 7): an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Not in the paper: the unbalanced tensors T_{a,b,c}, fields of positive characteristic, the bound for T_{1,1,c}, the optimality within the family, Proposition 4.

sources.title: Fast Structured Matrix Computations: Tensor Rank and Cohn–Umans Method
sources.note: Background, context only: Theorem 14.1 of arXiv:1601.00292v2, p. 27 (the journal text was not read): over ℂ, the symmetric matrix–vector product (diagonal included) has rank n(n+1)/2. The zero-diagonal case, T_{1,1,c} with n = c + 2 (Remark 1 of the README), is not treated there.

sources.title: Product Ranks of the 3 × 3 Determinant and Permanent
sources.note: Background: Remark 2.2 of arXiv:1503.00822v2, p. 4 (the journal text was not read), the tensor rank of the 3 × 3 permanent (= T_{1,1,1} = P_1) is 4, over fields of characteristic 0.

sources.title: The rank of the 5×5 permanent tensor is sixteen
sources.note: Background: pp. 2–3 report that the 3 × 3 permanent has rank and border rank 4 over fields of characteristic 0 (border rank ≥ 4: Derksen–Makam 2019, not read directly; the value with Fischer's formula).
